patterns.title: Seeking the Wrong Goal
patterns.domain: Systems and feedback traps; operational objectives, proxy measures, service purpose, allocation, and outcome evaluation

sources.author: Donella H. Meadows
sources.title: Thinking in Systems: A Primer
sources.read_method: Opened and read Seeking the Wrong Goal, printed pages 138–141 (PDF pages 154–157), including the distinction between following a misdefined goal and evading a rule.
sources.supports: Named system trap, goal sensitivity of feedback, effort/output versus intended result, and the contrast with Rule Beating.
sources.boundary: Foundational qualitative structural account, not a universal empirical law or theorem. Historical claims elsewhere in the chapter are not imported as verified case outcomes. The article does not claim Meadows originated all prior research on performance measures.

sources.author: Donald T. Campbell
sources.title: Assessing the Impact of Planned Social Change
sources.read_method: Opened the complete original occasional paper, dated December 1976, and read the Corrupting Effect of Quantitative Indicators discussion, printed pages 49–52, including the stated evidential limits and the employment-services illustration.
sources.supports: Earlier warning about consequential indicators distorting the processes they describe; reported shift toward easier placements when placement counts determine evaluation.
sources.boundary: Campbell describes his supporting evidence as predominantly anecdotal. The employment-services illustration reports earlier studies rather than a new controlled experiment in this paper. It is not used to estimate prevalence, quantify an intervention effect, or establish a universal mathematical law. Controversial military and industrial examples are not imported.

sources.author: U.S. Government Accountability Office
sources.title: Performance Measurement and Evaluation: Definitions and Relationships, GAO-11-646SP
sources.read_method: Opened and read the full accessible report, released May 20, 2011, especially the definitions of process/output/outcome measures and the complementary roles of performance measurement, outcome evaluation and impact evaluation.
sources.supports: Operational distinctions among activities, services delivered and their results, and why routine performance monitoring does not alone isolate program contribution.
sources.boundary: Official methodological guidance, not evidence that the support-service intervention has a measured effect. Measuring an outcome and attributing a net impact remain distinct.

sources.author: Australian Bureau of Statistics
sources.title: Measures of GDP, Australian System of National Accounts: Concepts, Sources and Methods, Edition 8
sources.read_method: Opened and read the official methodology page, released January 20, 2026, especially section 8.20 on the purpose and welfare limitations of GDP.
sources.supports: GDP is a production measure; production matters to welfare but does not comprehensively represent it. A valid statistic can be misused as an exhaustive objective.
sources.boundary: Documented measurement scope, not a causal estimate that economic growth fails to help welfare or that a particular replacement indicator is superior.

patterns.short_description: Recognize when a system is successfully producing a measured result that does not serve its purpose, then revise the objective, evidence, and constraints that direct decisions.
use_when: Which objective determines what staff actually do?
goals: Recognize the concrete predicament before terminology.
Preserve defining assumptions and distinctions without calculations.
Evaluate intervention authority, costs, residual risks, and changed assumptions.
mechanisms: Make substantive resolution govern decisions, with meaningful access and quality constraints.
Longer calls can increase waiting. No single score settles capacity, hard-case access, or the meaning of resolution.

example_structure.scenario: Accurate duration data and sincere management priorities can favor calls ending over problems being resolved, without individual bonuses or fabricated closure. Repeat contacts linked to unresolved cases; calls are events, cases can accumulate. Revised purpose and decision rule preserve safety, access, and difficult cases while acknowledging finite staff time.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Make substantive resolution govern decisions, with meaningful access and quality constraints.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Longer calls can increase waiting. No single score settles capacity, hard-case access, or the meaning of resolution.
example_structure.evidence: Hypothetical scenario and stipulated continuation; no expected result presented as measured outcome. Qualitative ranking and ordering replace illustrative arithmetic.

visual.question: Which objective determines what staff actually do?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. A shortest-call objective favors brief explanations and early endings even when call times are accurate. Some problems remain and generate repeat contact. A revised resolution objective authorizes necessary work and links contacts to cases, while preserving safety, accessibility, and difficult cases. Change: Make substantive resolution govern decisions, with meaningful access and quality constraints. Limitation: Longer calls can increase waiting. No single score settles capacity, hard-case access, or the meaning of resolution.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. Both procedures use the same staff time. Green changes the authorized objective and decision rule, not reporting accuracy or an individual bonus. More complete calls may leave fewer slots for new callers, and counted closure still needs verification.

patterns.evidence_boundary: Foundational definitions and formal results retain their assumptions. Empirical studies retain setting and design limitations. Examples and suggested practical responses are original editorial synthesis. Expected familiarity is an editorial judgment, not a comprehension-study finding.
